title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: many customers with mixed short/long LLM workloads are not getting ideal unit economics because defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching were conservative, and quantization recommendation plumbing didn't expose sensible profiles to the platform. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) new autotune defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching based on workload shape telemetry; 2) a small set of vetted quantization profiles (int8, int4-high, int4-safe) with model-compatibility checks and fallback rules; 3) unit-economics tooling in the console/backend to simulate expected cost/latency tradeoffs and export recommended configuration bundles.
commits: init: add autotune defaults module and config schema
feat(runtime): implement workload-shape based batch sizing and dynamic windowing
feat(cache): KV/prefix caching heuristics + eviction policy tuning
feat(quant): add quant profiles registry + compatibility checks
chore(ui): unit-econ simulation endpoint and console widget
test: add integration tests for batching + cache + quant interplay
docs: document new defaults and profiles
fix: throttle fallback to unquantized model when perf regressed
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall LGTM. Two requests: (1) add a safety valve in scheduler when tail-latency > target, (2) add a short note in docs about model family compatibility for int4-high.
Maya Chen: Added safety valve with a dynamic max-batch cap and documented int4-high compatibility in docs (see commit 'fix: throttle fallback...').
Lena Ortiz: CI initially failed on quant profile matrix; tests now pass after fixing a seed-dependent test. Please ensure we have a flaky test ticket if it reappears.
Noah Brooks (approver): Verified e2e in perf lab -- median token cost improved ~18% for mixed chat workloads and tail p99 increased <5ms. Approving to merge.
SRE note (automated): Observability hooks added for rollout. Recommend canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 24h before 100%.
Security (quick review): No new secrets or KMS changes. Quant profiles are metadata-only; OK to proceed.
ci_summary: CI pipeline: autotune_integration (flaky) - initial run failed on quant matrix
Checks: lint - pass, unit - pass, integration - pass, e2e-perf (lab) - pass
performance_results: Mixed chat workload (50/50 short/long): median token cost -18.3%
Batching-only microbenchmark: throughput +22% at 95th percentile load
Tail latency (p99) change: +4.6ms on average across tested models
Quantized (int4-safe) accuracy regression: <0.7% in classification evals; int4-high ~1.6% on sensitive prompts, auto-fallback enabled
rollout_plan: Canary 5% traffic for 24h: metrics to monitor = token_cost, p99_latency, model_quality_regressions
If cost improves and p99 < baseline+10ms and quality regressions < 2% -> ramp to 50% over 12h
Automatic rollback on >5% quality regressions or >20% p99 increase
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching/caching, introduce three quantization profiles with compatibility checks, and add unit-economics simulator in Console. Expected median token cost savings for mixed workloads: ~15-20%. Can be rolled out gradually with canary controls.
notes: Backported: none (changes touch runtime and console).
Docs: ops and quantization guides updated; update customer-facing FAQ after GA.
Follow-ups: ENG-3250 track flaky quant matrix test; ENG-3261 add telemetry for quant fallback frequency
